```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
pal <- c(navy = "#2b3a67", teal = "#2a9d8f", orange = "#e76f51",
         gold = "#e9c46a", grey = "#bbbbbb")
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 15))
set.seed(2026)
```

## The week {.smaller}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 5.2
blocks <- tribble(
  ~day, ~half, ~label, ~kind,
  "Mon", "AM", "Welcome\nKeynote\nWet lab", "other",
  "Mon", "PM", "Reads to\ncount tables", "lecture",
  "Tue", "AM", "Count table\nanatomy", "module",
  "Tue", "PM", "Differential\ntesting", "module",
  "Wed", "AM", "Group\nproject I", "project",
  "Wed", "PM", "Distances and\nordination", "module",
  "Thu", "AM", "Group\nproject II", "project",
  "Thu", "PM", "Sets and\nenrichment", "module",
  "Fri", "AM", "Integration\n+ presentations", "lecture",
  "Fri", "PM", "Keynote\nCertificates", "other"
) |>
  mutate(x = match(day, c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri")),
         y = if_else(half == "AM", 2, 1))

ggplot(blocks, aes(x, y, fill = kind)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 3, width = 0.97, height = 0.95) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), colour = "white", size = 4.6, lineheight = 0.95,
            fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(module = pal[["navy"]], lecture = pal[["teal"]],
                               project = pal[["orange"]], other = pal[["grey"]])) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:5, labels = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri"),
                     position = "top") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(2, 1), labels = c("AM", "PM")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_void(base_size = 17) +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "grey25"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 1, margin = margin(r = 8)),
        legend.position = "none")
```

Four coding modules. Two group project sessions. Everything else is talking.

## One idea holds the week together {.center}

. . .

Human gene expression and bacterial communities arrive as **the same kind of
object**: a table of counts.

. . .

Learn the table once, and you can analyse both.

## Two tables, one shape

```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 5
grid_plot <- function(n_row, n_col, title, subtitle, fill) {
  expand_grid(r = seq_len(n_row), c = seq_len(n_col)) |>
    mutate(v = runif(n())) |>
    ggplot(aes(c, -r, fill = v)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = fill) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_void(base_size = 15) +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 17),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35"))
}
grid_plot(10, 14, "Bacterial species", "220 rows x 471 columns", pal[["teal"]]) +
  grid_plot(10, 14, "Human genes", "14,226 rows x 471 columns", pal[["orange"]])
```

Rows are features. Columns are samples. Cells are counts of sequencing reads.

## The same five questions, twice {.smaller}

| | you will ask it of species | and of genes |
|---|---|---|
| How much did we sequence? | library size | library size |
| What is here at all? | prevalence | expression level |
| Which features differ between groups? | differential abundance | differential expression |
| How similar are two samples? | beta diversity | sample distance |
| What do the hits have in common? | taxonomy | gene sets |

: {tbl-colwidths="[28,36,36]"}

## The study we will work on {.smaller}

A pregnancy cohort. 157 participants, sampled three times.

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- **weeks 18, 24 and 34** of pregnancy
- **cervicovaginal samples** at each visit
- **two measurements** per sample: bacterial 16S and human gene expression
- **one outcome** per person: term or preterm birth
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
tibble(visit = c("week 18", "week 24", "week 34")) |>
  mutate(x = row_number()) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, 1)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 1, xend = 3, y = 1, yend = 1), colour = pal[["grey"]], linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(size = 16, colour = pal[["navy"]]) +
  geom_text(aes(label = visit), vjust = 3.2, size = 5) +
  annotate("text", x = 3.6, y = 1, label = "birth", size = 5, fontface = "bold",
           colour = pal[["orange"]]) +
  annotate("segment", x = 3.15, xend = 3.4, y = 1, yend = 1,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm")), colour = pal[["orange"]], linewidth = 1.2) +
  xlim(0.7, 3.9) +
  theme_void()
```
:::
:::

## Say this out loud once {.center}

These data are **constructed**.

. . .

The sequencing is real. Every count in both tables came off a real machine from
a real sample.

. . .

The study around it, the visit labels and the birth outcomes, is ours. We built
it so the week has something worth finding.

. . .

So: do the analysis properly, and do not cite the result.

## How the days are built

::: {.incremental}
- **One hour** of us talking, with code on the screen
- **Ninety minutes** of you writing code
- Two exercises per module, discussion in between
:::

. . .

You will have an AI coding agent the whole time. Every exercise ends by asking
you to check what it did.
